docs.title: Welcome To V-90
docs.text: V-90 is a set of five audio plug-ins that bring the effect programs of a classic late-1980s digital multi-effects unit to your DAW. Each plug-in has the unit's front panel: the same programs, the same parameters and ranges, and the same LCD text.

docs.title: The V-90 Plug-Ins
docs.text:
Plug-in Programs (memory numbers) V-90 Symphonic 15 Symphonic V-90 Reverbs 1 Rev 1 Hall, 2 Rev 2 Room, 3 Rev 3 Vocal, 4 Rev 4 Plate, 20 Reverb & Gate V-90 Reflections 5 Early Ref. 1, 6 Early Ref. 2, 16 Gate Reverb, 17 Reverse Gate V-90 Modulations 7 Delay L,R, 8 Stereo Echo, 9 Stereo Flange A, 10 Stereo Flange B, 11 Chorus A, 12 Chorus B, 13 Stereo Phasing, 14 Tremolo, 27 Auto Pan, 29 Delay Vibrato V-90 Pitch Change 21 Pitch Change A, 22 Pitch Change B, 23 Pitch Change C, 24 Pitch Change D

The V-90 Complete installer installs all five plug-ins. See the Memory List for every program in memory order.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• The original programs, with the unit's parameters, value steps and factory settings.
  • A front panel that works like the hardware: PARAMETER, BALANCE, MEMORY and RECALL keys, a two-line LCD and a memory display.
  • Each memory keeps its own settings while you try others.
  • Every parameter can be automated, and the parameters that are lists or switches (such as Memory and Bypass) show as lists or switches in your DAW.
  • MIDI control: play Pitch Change A and D from a keyboard, and trigger Reverb & Gate and Delay Vibrato with MIDI notes.
  • Mono-to-stereo and stereo-to-stereo.
  • AAX Native, AAX DSP (except V-90 Reflections), AU, VST 3 and, on Windows, VST.
  • A resizable window.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
• Quick Start Guide: up and running in a few minutes.
  • Installation and Activating the License.
  • The V-90 Panel: what each control does.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text:
1. Install. Run the V-90 Complete installer for your computer. See Installation.
  2. Insert a plug-in. In your DAW, insert a V-90 plug-in on a mono or stereo track, or on a stereo aux/bus used as an effect return. The plug-ins are listed under Neyrinck Audio and in the Reverb, Modulation, Delay and Pitch Shift categories.
  3. License. The first time the plug-in opens, the iLok licensing window appears. Select Activate if you have a license, or Try to start a trial. See Activating the License.
  4. Set the input level. Play audio and turn the INPUT knob so the meter peaks in the green, with only occasional orange. The knob's default (8) is unity gain.
  5. Choose a program. Press the MEMORY ▲/▼ keys (right of the BALANCE key). The memory number blinks and the LCD shows the program's name. Press RECALL to load it.
  6. Edit. Press PARAMETER to step through the program's parameters, and the ▲/▼ keys next to it to change the value shown on the LCD. You can also drag on the LCD, or click it to type a value.
  7. Set the balance. Press BALANCE and set the dry/effect mix. On an effect return, set BALANCE to 100 %.

Tip

Option-click (Alt-click on Windows) the LCD to return the parameter shown to its factory value.

docs.title: Using V-90 as an Effect Return
docs.text:
1. Create a stereo aux or bus track and insert the V-90 plug-in on it.
  2. Send to it from the tracks you want to process.
  3. Set BALANCE to 100 % so the return carries only the effect.

docs.title: Using V-90 as an Insert
docs.text: Insert the plug-in directly on the track and use BALANCE to set how much effect you hear. A mono track becomes stereo after the plug-in.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The V-90 Complete installer installs all five V-90 plug-ins: Symphonic, Reverbs, Reflections, Modulations and Pitch Change.

Platform Formats installed macOS AAX, AU, VST 3 Windows AAX, VST 3, VST

The AAX plug-ins include AAX Native and, for Symphonic, Reverbs, Modulations and Pitch Change, AAX DSP for Pro Tools HDX systems.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Download the installer. Use a web browser to open the Neyrinck V-90 page and download the installer for your computer.
  2. Quit your DAW and close all other running apps.
  3. Run the installer and follow the steps. It installs the plug-ins in the standard plug-in folders, and the shared V-90 graphics they need.
  4. Launch your DAW. The plug-ins appear under the manufacturer name Neyrinck Audio.

Note

The V-90 Complete installer installs over earlier V-90 Symphonic, Reverbs and Pitch Change releases.

docs.title: Plug-In Locations
docs.text:
macOSWindows Format Folder AAX /Library/Application Support/Avid/Audio/Plug-Ins AU /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components VST 3 /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3 Format Folder AAX C:\Program Files\Common Files\Avid\Audio\Plug-Ins VST 3 C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3 VST The VST folder you choose during installation

The shared graphics are installed in C:\ProgramData\Neyrinck\V-90\Resources.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: Delete the V-90 plug-ins from the folders above.

docs.title: Activating the License
docs.text: The V-90 plug-ins use iLok licensing. A license can be activated on your computer or on an iLok USB key, which makes it easy to move the license between computers. You can learn more at ilok.com.

docs.title: Activate a License
docs.text:
1. Launch your DAW and insert a V-90 plug-in.
  2. When the licensing window appears, select Activate.
  3. Enter your iLok ID and password.
  4. Select the V-90 license and select Next.
  5. Choose the location for the license: your computer or an iLok USB key.

The plug-in is now licensed and ready to use.

docs.title: Try Before You Buy
docs.text: If you do not have a license, select Try in the licensing window of any V-90 plug-in. This puts a V-90 Complete trial in your iLok account: trial licenses for all four V-90 licenses, so you can try all five plug-ins.

V-90 Complete is all four licenses sold together. When you buy V-90 Complete, your iLok account receives the four licenses above. Activate each one as described above.

docs.text:
On Pro Tools HDX systems, these plug-ins can run on the DSP:

docs.title: Track Formats
docs.text: The plug-ins are mono-to-stereo and stereo-to-stereo. See Signal Flow and Track Formats.

docs.title: V-90 Modulations
docs.text:
V-90 Modulations has the original unit's delay and modulation programs: stereo delays and echoes, flangers, choruses, phasing, tremolo, auto pan and a delayed vibrato.

Memory Program Character 7 Delay L,R Independent left and right delays, up to 500 ms. 8 Stereo Echo Left and right echoes with feedback, up to 250 ms. 9 Stereo Flange A Stereo flanger. 10 Stereo Flange B Stereo flanger: a slow, deep sweep. 11 Chorus A Stereo chorus. 12 Chorus B Stereo chorus, faster and with less level modulation. 13 Stereo Phasing Stereo phaser. 14 Tremolo Level modulation. 27 Auto Pan Automatic panning. 29 Delay Vibrato A vibrato that starts after a delay and fades in, as a singer's does.

Choose a program with the MEMORY keys and RECALL. See Memories and Recall.

docs.title: Delay L,R
docs.text:
Two delays, one for each output. In Delay L,R, the left and right echoes feed back into each other.

Rch DLY Delay R 0.1 ms – 500.0 ms 200.0 ms Right channel delay time. Rch F.B Feedback R -99 % – +99 % +0 % Right channel feedback: the number of repeats. Negative values invert the polarity of the feedback. HIGH High 0.1 – 1.0 1.0 High-frequency damping of the repeats: lower values make each repeat darker. 1.0 is no damping. BALANCE Balance 0 % – 100 % 100 % Mix of dry and effect sound. 0 % is dry only, 100 % is effect only. Use 100 % when the plug-in is on an effect return.

docs.text:

VIB DLY Vibrato Delay 1 ms – 12001 ms 400 ms Time from the trigger to the start of the vibrato. VIB RISE Attack 5 ms – 32000 ms 1400 ms Time the vibrato takes to reach full depth. VIB FRQ Mod Freq 0.1 Hz – 20.0 Hz 7.0 Hz Vibrato speed. VIB DEPTH Mod Depth 0 % – 100 % 40 % Vibrato depth. MIDI TRG. MIDI Trigger Off, On On When ON, a MIDI note-on triggers the effect instead of the input level. BALANCE Balance 0 % – 100 % 100 % Mix of dry and effect sound. 0 % is dry only, 100 % is effect only. Use 100 % when the plug-in is on an effect return.

docs.title: AAX DSP
docs.text: V-90 Modulations runs as AAX Native and AAX DSP. On DSP it needs one DSP chip at 96 kHz.

docs.title: V-90 Pitch Change
docs.text:
V-90 Pitch Change has the original unit's four pitch-shifting programs: for harmonies, doubling, detuning and special effects.

Memory Program Character 21 Pitch Change A One shifted voice, with feedback. Can be played from a MIDI keyboard. 22 Pitch Change B Two shifted voices, mixed to both outputs. 23 Pitch Change C Two shifted voices, one on the left output and one on the right. 24 Pitch Change D One shifted voice with feedback, like A, with a different pitch-shifting method. Can be played from a MIDI keyboard.

V-90 Pitch Change starts with Pitch Change C, whose factory setting detunes the left and right sides slightly up and down for a wide doubling effect.

Choose a program with the MEMORY keys and RECALL. See Memories and Recall.

docs.title: Pitch Change A and D
docs.text:
One pitch-shifted voice. F.B. GAIN feeds the shifted voice back into the shifter, so each repeat is shifted again: with a DELAY, this gives rising or falling arpeggio effects.

With BASE KEY on, MIDI notes set PITCH. See MIDI Control.

Parameter (LCD) Host name Range Default Description PITCH Pitch 1 -12 – +12 +0 Pitch shift in semitones, ±1 octave. FINE Fine 1 -100 – +100 +0 Fine pitch shift, in cents (1/100 semitone). DELAY Delay 1 0.1 ms – 400.0 ms 0.1 ms Delay of the shifted voice. F.B. GAIN Feedback Gain 0 % – 99 % 0 % Feedback: how much of the effect is fed back into it. Higher values give a more pronounced, resonant effect. BASE KEY Base Key Off, C1 – C6 C3 The MIDI note that plays the pitch unshifted. A MIDI note sets PITCH to its distance from BASE KEY. OFF ignores MIDI notes. See MIDI Control. BALANCE Balance 0 % – 100 % 100 % Mix of dry and effect sound. 0 % is dry only, 100 % is effect only. Use 100 % when the plug-in is on an effect return.

docs.title: Pitch Change B
docs.text:

docs.title: V-90 Reflections
docs.text:
V-90 Reflections has the original unit's early-reflection programs. Instead of a smooth reverb tail, they produce a pattern of distinct reflections: for ambience, room sound, and the gated and reverse effects of the 1980s.

Memory Program Character 5 Early Ref. 1 Early reflections of a room, hall or plate. 6 Early Ref. 2 A second early-reflection program with the same controls and a different sound. 16 Gate Reverb A dense burst of reflections that stops abruptly, like a gated reverb. 17 Reverse Gate Reflections that build up instead of dying away, like a reversed reverb.

All four programs have the same parameters, with their own factory settings.

LIVENESS Liveness 0 – 10 5 Decay of the reflections: 0 is a dead room (the reflections die away), 10 a live room (they stay strong). DELAY Delay 0.1 ms – 400.0 ms 10.0 ms Initial delay before the reflections start. LPF Low Pass 1.0 kHz – Thru Thru Low-pass filter on the effect sound. THRU is off. BALANCE Balance 0 % – 100 % 100 % Mix of dry and effect sound. 0 % is dry only, 100 % is effect only. Use 100 % when the plug-in is on an effect return.

docs.title: V-90 Reverbs
docs.text:
V-90 Reverbs has the original unit's reverb programs: four classic reverbs and a gated reverb.

Choose a program with the MEMORY keys and RECALL. See Memories and Recall.

docs.title: Reverb & Gate
docs.text:
A reverb whose output passes through a gate. When the input level reaches TRG. LEVEL, the gate opens, stays open for HOLD, then closes over RELEASE. With a short HOLD and RELEASE, a long reverb is cut off abruptly: the classic gated snare.

With MIDI TRG. set to ON, MIDI notes open the gate instead of the input level. See MIDI Control.

Parameter (LCD) Host name Range Default Description REV TIME Rev Time 0.3 s – 99.0 s 2.0 s Reverb time: how long the reverb takes to decay by 60 dB. HIGH High 0.1 – 1.0 0.6 High-frequency reverb time, as a ratio of REV TIME. Lower values make the highs die away sooner, for a darker, more natural decay. DELAY Delay 0.1 ms – 50.0 ms 10.0 ms Initial delay before the reverb starts. HPF High Pass Thru – 1.0 kHz Thru High-pass filter on the effect sound. THRU is off. LPF Low Pass 1.0 kHz – Thru Thru Low-pass filter on the effect sound. THRU is off. TRG. LEVEL Trigger Level 1 – 100 65 Input level that triggers the effect. Lower values trigger on quieter signals. HOLD Hold 1 ms – 12001 ms 150 ms How long the gate stays open after it is triggered. RELEASE Release 5 ms – 32000 ms 5 ms How long the gate takes to close after HOLD. MIDI TRG. MIDI Trigger Off, On Off When ON, a MIDI note-on triggers the effect instead of the input level. BALANCE Balance 0 % – 100 % 100 % Mix of dry and effect sound. 0 % is dry only, 100 % is effect only. Use 100 % when the plug-in is on an effect return.

docs.text: V-90 Reverbs runs as AAX Native and AAX DSP. On DSP it needs one DSP chip at 96 kHz.

docs.title: V-90 Symphonic
docs.text:
V-90 Symphonic is memory 15 of the original unit: the Symphonic effect, a rich, wide, multi-voice chorus. It thickens and spreads anything from guitars and keyboards to vocals and strings, and turns a mono source into a lush stereo one.

V-90 Symphonic has one program, so its panel has no MEMORY keys or RECALL key. It is simple to adjust with three parameters.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Press PARAMETER to switch between MOD. FRQ and MOD. DEPTH, and BALANCE to select BALANCE.

Parameter (LCD) Host name Range Default Description MOD. FRQ Frequency 0.1 – 40.0 Hz 0.7 Hz Modulation speed. MOD. DEPTH Depth 0 – 100 % 50 % Modulation depth. BALANCE Balance 0 – 100 % 100 % Mix of dry and effect sound. Use 100 % on an effect return.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Slow speeds (below 1 Hz) and moderate depth give the classic wide, shimmering sound.
  • For a subtle widening on a lead vocal, use it on an effect return and blend it in with the send level.
  • Higher speeds give a vibrato-like warble.

docs.title: AAX DSP
docs.text: V-90 Symphonic runs as AAX Native and AAX DSP on Pro Tools HDX systems.

docs.title: Version 1.1.0.4
docs.text:
• AAX DSP for V-90 Reverbs, V-90 Pitch Change and V-90 Modulations, as for V-90 Symphonic: on Pro Tools HDX systems they can run on the DSP. Each needs one DSP chip at 96 kHz.
  • On DSP, Reverbs takes a parameter change 4 samples later than AAX Native does, and a Memory change is silent for about 0.2 ms; Pitch Change's Memory change is silent for about 33 ms.
  • Memory, Reflections' Type, Modulations' Direction and Pitch Change's Base Key are now discrete parameters, and MIDI Trigger and Bypass are on/off switches, so hosts show them as lists or switches and never ramp them.
  • A Memory now starts from its current settings when it was changed while another Memory played or while bypassed.

Known issues

  • V-90 Reflections is AAX Native only (no AAX DSP).
  • AU automation recorded with earlier versions on the parameters that are now discrete may play back rescaled.
  • VST automation in sessions saved with 1.1.0.2 may not match its parameters, which have changed.

docs.title: Version 1.1.0.3
docs.text:
New plug-ins in addition to V-90 Symphonic

  • V-90 Reverbs: Rev 1 Hall, Rev 2 Room, Rev 3 Vocal, Rev 4 Plate and Reverb & Gate.
  • V-90 Reflections: Early Ref. 1, Early Ref. 2, Gate Reverb and Reverse Gate.
  • V-90 Pitch Change: Pitch Change A, B, C and D. Pitch Change A and D follow MIDI notes (BASE KEY).
  • V-90 Modulations: Delay L,R, Stereo Echo, Stereo Flange A and B, Chorus A and B, Stereo Phasing, Tremolo, Auto Pan and Delay Vibrato. Delay Vibrato can be triggered by MIDI notes.

The V-90 Complete installer installs all five, as AAX, AU and VST 3 on macOS and AAX, VST and VST 3 on Windows.

Changes since 1.1.0.2

  • Reverbs, Reflections, Pitch Change and Modulations no longer have an Out Level parameter; it is fixed at 100 %, as in Symphonic.
  • Their parameters start with Memory, Input and Balance and end with Bypass, and are named in title case ("Room Size").
  • They are listed in more specific host categories: Reverb, Pitch Shift, and Modulation and Delay.
  • Smaller plug-ins.

docs.title: Version 1.1.0.1
docs.text:
• Every V-90 plug-in now shares one version number.
  • New plug-ins: V-90 Reverbs, V-90 Pitch Change and V-90 Modulations.

docs.title: V-90 Symphonic 1.0.2.3
docs.text:
• Smaller download: the plug-ins are about a third of their previous size.
  • Fixed a short fade-in when playback or rendering starts.
  • Improved AAX compatibility: the AAX Native and AudioSuite plug-ins no longer declare DSP-only settings.

docs.title: V-90 Symphonic 1.0.2
docs.text: • Fixed a short fade-in when playback or rendering starts.

docs.title: V-90 Symphonic 1.0.1
docs.text: • Fixed AAX DSP loading on Mac.

docs.title: The plug-in window shows only a message about missing files
docs.text: The plug-ins share their panel graphics, which the installer puts in a common folder. If those files are missing, the window shows what is missing instead of the panel. Run the V-90 Complete installer again.

docs.title: The plug-in does not appear in my DAW
docs.text:
• Check that your DAW supports one of the installed formats: AAX (Pro Tools), AU (macOS), VST 3, or VST (Windows).
  • Rescan plug-ins in your DAW, or restart it.
  • Look under the manufacturer name Neyrinck Audio, or in the Reverb, Modulation, Delay and Pitch Shift categories.

docs.title: The licensing window appears every time
docs.text: The plug-in cannot find a license. Make sure the iLok USB key holding the license is connected, or that the license is activated on this computer, using iLok License Manager. See Activating the License.

docs.title: I hear no effect
docs.text:
• Check that BYPASS is off (its light is off).
  • Check BALANCE: at 0 % you hear only the dry signal.
  • Check the INPUT knob and the meter: at 0 there is no signal.
  • Reverb & Gate and Delay Vibrato are triggered effects. Check TRG. LEVEL, or, with MIDI TRG. ON, that MIDI notes reach the plug-in. See MIDI Control.

docs.title: My stereo track sounds mono at BALANCE 0 %
docs.text: This is how the original unit works: the input is summed to mono. Use BYPASS to hear the original stereo input. See Signal Flow and Track Formats.

docs.title: Pitch Change does not follow my MIDI notes
docs.text:
• Only Pitch Change A and D follow MIDI notes.
  • Check that BASE KEY is not OFF.
  • Check that the MIDI track's output is set to the plug-in.

docs.title: My edits to a program came back after switching programs
docs.text: That is by design: each memory keeps its own settings. To return a memory to its factory settings, press RECALL while it plays, without choosing another memory first. See Memories and Recall.

docs.title: Contact Support
docs.text: If you need further help, contact Neyrinck support through neyrinck.com.

docs.title: Automation
docs.text: Every V-90 parameter can be automated and controlled from a control surface.

docs.title: Parameter Order
docs.text:
The parameters appear in your DAW in this order:

  1. Memory (not in V-90 Symphonic)
  2. Input
  3. Balance
  4. The program parameters, named in title case (for example, "Rev Time", "Room Size", "Mod Depth")
  5. Bypass

Each plug-in page lists the host name of every parameter.

docs.title: Lists and Switches
docs.text:
These parameters are discrete: your DAW shows them as lists or on/off switches and never ramps between values.

  • Memory
  • Reflections' Type
  • Modulations' Direction (Auto Pan)
  • Pitch Change's Base Key
  • MIDI Trigger (Reverb & Gate, Delay Vibrato)
  • Bypass

docs.title: Automation and Memories
docs.text:
The parameters you automate are the playing memory's. When automation changes Memory, the new memory's own settings come in. An automation point on another parameter at the same moment as the memory change applies to the new memory.

Tip

To switch between programs during a song, automate Memory, then write each memory's settings while it plays.

docs.title: Values Are the Unit's Steps
docs.text: Each parameter moves in the original unit's steps. Your DAW shows the value as the unit does, for example 2.6s or 8.0 kHz.

docs.title: Memories and Recall
docs.text: V-90 Reverbs, Reflections, Modulations and Pitch Change each hold several programs. As on the original unit, each program is a memory with its own number, shown on the MEMORY display.

docs.title: Choosing a Memory
docs.text:
1. Press MEMORY ▲ or MEMORY ▼. The memory number blinks, the LCD shows the program's name, and the RECALL light comes on. The program you were playing keeps playing.
  2. Keep pressing the MEMORY keys until you reach the program you want. They wrap around from the last memory to the first.
  3. Press RECALL to load it.

To leave without changing the program, press PARAMETER, BALANCE or ▲/▼, or step back to the playing memory.

docs.title: Each Memory Keeps Its Settings
docs.text:
Every memory remembers its own parameter values. If you edit Rev 1 Hall, switch to Rev 4 Plate and later come back to Rev 1 Hall, your Rev 1 Hall settings are still there. All the memories' settings are saved with your session.

The parameters your DAW shows are always those of the playing memory. A change from the panel, from automation or from a control surface goes to the playing memory.

docs.title: Returning to the Factory Settings
docs.text:
• One parameter: Option-click (Alt-click on Windows) the LCD to return the parameter shown to its factory value.
  • The whole memory: press RECALL without choosing another memory first. All of the playing memory's parameters return to their factory values. Your DAW can undo this.

docs.title: Changing Memory from the DAW
docs.text:
Memory is also a parameter (Memory) that you can automate or set from your DAW's controls. It shows as a list of the programs. Changing it from anywhere brings in that memory's own settings.

Note

V-90 Symphonic has a single program and no memories.

docs.title: MIDI Control
docs.text:
Some V-90 programs respond to MIDI notes, as on the original unit:

Program Plug-in What MIDI notes do Turn it on with Pitch Change A V-90 Pitch Change Set the pitch BASE KEY (not OFF) Pitch Change D V-90 Pitch Change Set the pitch BASE KEY (not OFF) Reverb & Gate V-90 Reverbs Open the gate MIDI TRG. = ON Delay Vibrato V-90 Modulations Start the vibrato MIDI TRG. = ON (the default)

docs.title: Playing the Pitch from a Keyboard
docs.text:
In Pitch Change A and D, a MIDI note sets PITCH to the note's distance in semitones from BASE KEY. With BASE KEY at C3 (the default), C3 plays the original pitch, G3 plays a fifth up and C2 an octave down. The pitch is limited to ±12 semitones.

Set BASE KEY to OFF to ignore MIDI notes.

The PITCH value the note sets shows on the LCD and in your DAW, so you can record it as automation.

Note

BASE KEY C3 is MIDI note 60 (middle C).

docs.title: Triggering with MIDI
docs.text: Reverb & Gate's gate and Delay Vibrato's vibrato are normally triggered by the input level (TRG. LEVEL). With MIDI TRG. set to ON, a MIDI note-on triggers them instead, at the exact time of the note. Use this to trigger the effect in time with the music, independently of the audio.

docs.title: Sending MIDI to the Plug-In
docs.text:
How you route MIDI to an effect plug-in depends on your DAW.

Pro ToolsOther DAWs
  1. Create a MIDI track.
  2. Set the MIDI track's output to the V-90 plug-in (it is listed by the plug-in's name and insert).
  3. Record or draw the notes on the MIDI track.

Route a MIDI track's output to the V-90 plug-in, if your DAW supports MIDI input to effect plug-ins. See your DAW's documentation for sending MIDI to an audio effect.

AAX DSP: MIDI control on AAX DSP is new in version 1.1.0.4.

docs.title: The V-90 Panel
docs.text:
Every V-90 plug-in has the same front panel. V-90 Symphonic has one program, so it has no MEMORY keys or RECALL key.

From left to right:

Control What it does INPUT Input level, from 0 to 10. 8 is unity gain, 10 is +6 dB. Info (the NEYRINCK V-90 logo) Click to show the plug-in's version. Click again to hide it. Meter Input level after the INPUT knob, from −30 to 0 dBFS. The top three segments are orange. MEMORY display The number of the playing program. It blinks while you choose another one with the MEMORY keys. LCD Top line: the program name. Bottom line: the parameter selected and its value. PARAMETER Steps through the program's parameters. Its light is on when a parameter is selected. ▲/▼ (left pair) Change the value of the parameter shown on the LCD. BALANCE Selects the BALANCE parameter (the dry/effect mix). Its light is on while BALANCE is selected. MEMORY ▲/▼ (right pair) Choose another program. RECALL Loads the program chosen with the MEMORY keys. See Memories and Recall. BYPASS Bypasses the effect. Its light is on while bypassed.

docs.title: Changing a Value
docs.text:
There are several ways to change the parameter shown on the LCD:

  • Click ▲ or ▼ to change it by one step. Hold the key down to repeat.
  • Drag up or down on ▲ or ▼ for larger changes.
  • Drag up or down on the LCD.
  • Click the LCD and type a value, then press Enter. Press Esc to cancel. You can type the value as it is shown on the LCD, or a number: typing 8k for a low-pass filter chooses 8.0 kHz, and a value between two steps chooses the nearest.
  • Option-click the LCD (Alt-click on Windows) to return the parameter to the playing program's factory value.

Each parameter has the same steps as the original unit. For example, REV TIME moves in 0.1 s steps up to 5 s and in larger steps above.

docs.title: INPUT Knob
docs.text:
The INPUT knob sets the level into the plug-in. Set it so the meter peaks near the top of the green segments. As on the original unit, the dry part of the BALANCE mix comes after the INPUT knob, so the knob changes the level of both the dry and the effect sound. BYPASS passes the input through unchanged.

Knob Gain 0 Off 2 −24 dB 4 −12 dB 6 −6 dB 8 0 dB (default) 10 +6 dB

docs.title: Resizing the Window
docs.text: Drag the bottom-right corner of the plug-in window to make it larger or smaller, from a quarter to four times its normal size. The plug-in remembers the size in the session.

docs.title: Track Formats
docs.text:
The V-90 plug-ins are:

  • Mono-to-stereo: insert on a mono track; the track becomes stereo after the plug-in.
  • Stereo-to-stereo: insert on a stereo track, aux or bus.

docs.title: Mono Input, Stereo Output
docs.text:
Like the original unit, each program has a mono input and a stereo output. On a stereo track, the plug-in sums the left and right inputs to mono before the effect. The stereo image you hear comes from the effect: the reverb, the left and right delays, the panning and so on.

 Left  ─┐                                       ┌─ Left
        ├─ sum ─ INPUT ─┬─ effect ─┬─ BALANCE ──┤
 Right ─┘               └── dry ───┘            └─ Right

At BALANCE 0 % you hear the dry signal: the mono sum, after the INPUT knob. Use BYPASS to hear the original stereo input unchanged.

docs.title: BALANCE and Effect Returns
docs.text:
BALANCE mixes the dry and effect sound:

Use BALANCE Effect return (aux or bus fed by sends) 100 % Insert on a track To taste

Some programs start with BALANCE below 100 % (Stereo Flange A at 50 %, Stereo Flange B at 75 %), as on the unit.

docs.title: Output Level
docs.text: The plug-ins have no output level control. The output is at the original unit's 100 % output level.
